cards.explanation: Execution is the entering into of the contract and comes before clearing. Margin is computed during clearing, after execution.
cards.originalText: execution.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Large global dealer banks are active across all major asset classes and supply most of the OTC derivatives market's liquidity.
cards.explanation: Large players are global dealer banks trading FX, interest rate, equity, commodity and credit derivatives. They are members of most exchanges and CCPs and provide the bulk of market liquidity.
cards.originalText: A large global bank, often known as a dealer, active across all major asset classes.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Sovereigns, supranational entities and multilateral development banks with high credit ratings are known for receiving but not posting collateral in OTC derivative transactions with banks, subject to possible rating triggers.
cards.explanation: Their exceptional credit quality has let them dictate one-way terms. Rating triggers may require them to post collateral if they are downgraded.
cards.originalText: Sovereigns, supranational entities, or multilateral development banks with high credit ratings.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Corporate end users are especially known for receiving but not posting collateral in OTC derivative transactions with banks.
cards.explanation: Corporates are typically unable or unwilling to post collateral, but they do not get one-way terms from banks. They simply remain uncollateralised, whereas sovereigns and supranationals receive collateral without posting.
cards.originalText: Corporate clients engaged in large‑scale hedging of operational risks.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Bilateral OTC trades in which a party does not post collateral fall into the category of uncollateralised OTC derivatives.
cards.explanation: The four categories are exchange-traded, OTC centrally cleared, OTC collateralised and OTC uncollateralised. Bilateral trades without collateral posting are the uncollateralised category, the riskiest of the four.
cards.originalText: Bilateral OTC uncollateralized derivatives.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Exchange-traded derivatives are traded without collateral being posted by the participants.
cards.explanation: Exchange-traded derivatives are settled daily with margin, so collateral is always posted.
cards.originalText: Exchange‑traded derivatives.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Centrally cleared OTC derivatives are traded without collateral being posted by the participants.
cards.explanation: Central clearing requires daily variation margin, so posting collateral is mandatory.
cards.originalText: OTC centrally cleared derivatives.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: For exchange-traded derivatives, margin must be posted against losses on a daily basis by all exchange members.
cards.explanation: Exchanges have central clearing functions, and variation margin is settled in cash every day. This applies to all members and underpins the exchange's clearing guarantee.
cards.originalText: Margin must be posted against losses on a daily basis by all exchange members.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: No collateral is posted on exchange-traded derivatives because these instruments are considered self-hedging.
cards.explanation: No self-hedging exemption exists. Counterparty risk on exchange-traded derivatives is controlled by daily margining.
cards.originalText: No collateral is posted because these instruments are considered self‑hedging.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: For exchange-traded derivatives, collateral is posted only at contract maturity to cover the final settlement amount.
cards.explanation: Margin on exchange-traded derivatives is posted against losses daily, not only at maturity.
cards.originalText: Collateral is posted only at contract maturity to cover the final settlement amount.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Exchange-traded derivatives require collateral in the form of physical assets at the initiation of the contract.
cards.explanation: Margin on exchange-traded derivatives is mainly posted in cash against daily losses. Physical assets are not the norm.
cards.originalText: Collateral in the form of physical assets is required at the initiation of the contract.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: For centrally cleared OTC derivatives, collateral in the form of variation margin is posted in cash on a daily basis by participants.
cards.explanation: A CCP collateralises cleared OTC trades daily with cash variation margin, as it does for exchange-traded contracts.
cards.originalText: Collateral in the form of variation margin is posted in cash on a daily basis by participants.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Parties to centrally cleared OTC derivatives post securities as collateral on an annual basis.
cards.explanation: Annual posting would leave exposures unmargined for far too long. Cleared OTC trades are margined daily with cash variation margin.
cards.originalText: Parties post securities as collateral on an annual basis.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Collateral is not typically required for centrally cleared OTC derivatives because the trades are bespoke.
cards.explanation: Cleared trades are always collateralised. Bespoke trades that do not receive collateral are the bilateral uncollateralised case, not the centrally cleared one.
cards.originalText: Collateral is not typically required because the trades are bespoke.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: For centrally cleared OTC derivatives, a single upfront collateral payment is made at initiation and adjusted only at maturity.
cards.explanation: A CCP marks positions to market and collects variation margin daily. A single upfront payment adjusted only at maturity ignores that daily margining.
cards.originalText: A single upfront collateral payment is made at initiation and adjusted at maturity.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: A futures contract requires daily margin posted against losses through the exchange's central clearing, whereas the collateral terms of a bilateral OTC swap are negotiated between the parties and may be limited or absent for an end user.
cards.explanation: Futures are margined daily by the clearing function. Bilateral OTC collateral depends on the agreement between the parties, and end users often cannot or will not post.
cards.originalText: The futures contract requires daily margin posted against losses via the exchange’s central clearing, whereas the OTC swap’s collateral terms are negotiated bilaterally and may be limited or absent for an end user.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Neither a futures contract nor a bilateral OTC swap needs collateral when the user is hedging rather than speculating.
cards.explanation: The purpose of the trade does not remove margin requirements on exchange-traded futures, which are margined daily whatever the motive.
cards.originalText: Neither the futures contract nor the swap needs collateral because Harder is hedging rather than speculating.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: A futures contract requires collateral only at initiation, whereas a bilateral OTC swap requires daily collateral.
cards.explanation: The pattern is reversed. Futures are margined daily, and bilateral swaps are not automatically margined daily.
cards.originalText: The futures contract requires collateral only at initiation, and the swap requires daily collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Identify the participants and describe the use of collateralization in the derivatives market.
cards.statement: Both a futures contract and a bilateral OTC swap must be margined daily in cash on identical terms.
cards.explanation: Identical daily cash terms apply only to cleared products. A bilateral swap with a bank has negotiated collateral terms that may be limited or absent.
cards.originalText: Both the futures contract and the swap must be margined daily in cash on identical terms.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement enumerates specific events, such as bankruptcy, that constitute a default.
cards.explanation: Default is defined contractually through a list of events of default, such as failure to pay and bankruptcy, rather than left to legal uncertainty.
cards.originalText: It enumerates specific events, such as bankruptcy, that constitute a default.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement initiates an automatic restructuring of the terms for distressed derivatives.
cards.explanation: Default under the agreement leads to termination and close-out, not to automatic restructuring of the trades.
cards.originalText: It initiates an automatic restructuring of the terms for distressed derivatives.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement provides a grace period for all defaults before any enforcement action.
cards.explanation: Grace periods apply only to some events, such as certain payment failures, not to all defaults.
cards.originalText: It provides a grace period for all defaults before any enforcement action.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement ensures equal profit distribution among counterparties in case of default.
cards.explanation: The agreement calculates a single net close-out amount. It does not distribute profits equally among counterparties.
cards.originalText: It ensures equal profit distribution among counterparties in case of default.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: A failure by a counterparty to meet its payment or delivery obligations is an event of default under the ISDA Master Agreement.
cards.explanation: Failure to pay or deliver is the first and most common event of default listed in the agreement.
cards.originalText: A failure to meet payment or delivery obligations by a counterparty.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: A significant fluctuation in the market value of the underlying asset is an event of default under the ISDA Master Agreement.
cards.explanation: Market moves change exposure and are handled through collateral and margin, not through a default event.
cards.originalText: A significant fluctuation in the market value of the underlying asset.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The initiation of a merger or acquisition process by either party is an event of default under the ISDA Master Agreement.
cards.explanation: A merger alone is not a default. Only a merger without assumption of the party's obligations is a listed event of default.
cards.originalText: The initiation of a merger or acquisition process by either party.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The introduction of new regulatory requirements affecting derivatives is an event of default under the ISDA Master Agreement.
cards.explanation: New regulation is not a failure by the counterparty and is not a listed event of default.
cards.originalText: The introduction of new regulatory requirements affecting the derivatives.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement consolidates all transactions referenced under it into a single net obligation.
cards.explanation: Multiple transactions under one Master Agreement form a single legal contract, so on default they are netted into one obligation, which reduces exposure.
cards.originalText: Consolidation of all referenced transactions into a single net obligation.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement prescribes standardised interest rates for all derivative contracts.
cards.explanation: Commercial terms such as rates are set in each trade confirmation. The Master Agreement standardises legal terms, not rates.
cards.originalText: Prescribed standardized interest rates for all derivative contracts.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement requires the use of a specific third-party valuation service for all transactions.
cards.explanation: The agreement does not mandate a particular valuation provider.
cards.originalText: The use of a specific third‑party valuation service for all transactions.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement specifies the mechanics of the close-out process in the event of default.
cards.explanation: The agreement defines how transactions are valued and settled on default, removing legal uncertainty about the close-out.
cards.originalText: It specifies mechanics around the close‑out process in the event of default.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement mandates a uniform haircut percentage for all types of collateral.
cards.explanation: Haircuts are negotiated in the credit support annex and differ by collateral type. None is mandated uniformly.
cards.originalText: It mandates a uniform haircut percentage for all types of collateral.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement automatically adjusts margin requirements based on market volatility.
cards.explanation: Margin terms are set contractually in the credit support annex. The Master Agreement does not adjust them automatically for volatility.
cards.originalText: It automatically adjusts the margin requirements based on market volatility.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement requires all derivative transactions to be settled in a single, predetermined currency.
cards.explanation: The settlement currency is specified per transaction in the confirmation and is not forced to one currency.
cards.originalText: It requires all derivative transactions to be settled in a single, predetermined currency.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: Under the ISDA Master Agreement, a breach of the agreement, including default under a specified transaction, is an event of default.
cards.explanation: Breach of agreement and default under a specified transaction are both enumerated events of default.
cards.originalText: The breach of a covenant related to a specified transaction within the agreement.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Define the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) Master Agreement, the risk-mitigating features it provides, and the default events it covers.
cards.statement: A downgrade of a counterparty's credit rating below a specified threshold is an event of default under the ISDA Master Agreement.
cards.explanation: A rating downgrade is not a listed event of default. It may instead trigger collateral terms in the credit support annex.
cards.originalText: The counterparty’s credit rating downgrade below a specified threshold.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Credit derivatives such as CDS are instrumental in transferring credit risk but inherently carry counterparty risk within the contractual framework.
cards.explanation: A CDS transfers the reference entity's credit risk to the protection seller, but the buyer is then exposed to the risk that the seller fails to perform.
cards.originalText: Credit derivatives, while instrumental in transferring credit risk, inherently carry counterparty risk within the contractual framework.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Credit derivatives such as CDS function exclusively to enhance investment returns, with negligible influence on a firm's credit risk profile.
cards.explanation: Credit derivatives are mainly used to hedge or transfer credit risk, so they materially change the credit risk profile. Return enhancement is a secondary use.
cards.originalText: Credit derivatives, such as CDS, function exclusively to enhance investment returns, with negligible influence on the firm’s credit risk profile.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Credit derivatives distribute credit risk so evenly across parties that the possibility of default becomes negligible.
cards.explanation: Risk is transferred, not eliminated. Default risk remains with the protection seller and the counterparty relationship.
cards.originalText: Credit derivatives, by design, distribute credit risk so evenly across parties that the possibility of default becomes negligible.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Credit derivatives are generally immune to market fluctuations, ensuring stable valuation and risk assessment.
cards.explanation: CDS values move with credit spreads and market conditions, which leads to mark-to-market changes and collateral calls.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Buying CDS protection transfers the reference entity's credit risk but introduces counterparty risk to the protection seller, which is most likely to be severe when the seller's credit quality is highly correlated with that of the reference entity.
cards.explanation: The seller's ability to pay is most in doubt exactly when the reference entity defaults. High correlation between the two makes this wrong-way risk.
cards.originalText: The CDS transfers the credit risk of Bank Z but introduces counterparty risk to Dealer Y, which is most likely to be severe exactly when Bank Z defaults and protection is needed.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: A CDS fully removes the credit risk of a position because the credit risk is transferred to the protection seller.
cards.explanation: The risk is transferred, not eliminated. The CDS contract embeds counterparty risk to the protection seller.
cards.originalText: The CDS fully removes credit risk from the position because the credit risk of Bank Z is transferred to Dealer Y.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Positive correlation between a reference entity and its CDS protection seller reduces the probability that both fail together, which makes the CDS a more effective hedge.
cards.explanation: Positive correlation raises, not lowers, the probability of joint failure. This makes the hedge less effective.
cards.originalText: The CDS is an effective hedge because the correlation between Bank Z and Dealer Y reduces the probability that both fail together.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: A CDS creates counterparty risk only if the protection seller is not a bank, because bank counterparties are default remote.
cards.explanation: Counterparty risk applies to any protection seller. Dealers proved not to be default remote in the 2008 crisis.
cards.originalText: The CDS creates counterparty risk only if Dealer Y is not a bank, because bank counterparties are default remote.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Credit derivatives are an efficient means of transferring credit risk, but if not used correctly they can be counterproductive, and the CDS contract itself contains counterparty risk.
cards.explanation: Credit derivatives transfer credit risk efficiently but can be highly toxic if misused, for example through speculation and leverage. A CDS also embeds counterparty risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Because the credit default swap is a complex instrument, its use has been confined to a few specialist dealers and it has had little effect on the trading of credit risk.
cards.explanation: The CDS is a simple core instrument that transformed credit risk trading, and its use was widespread before the global financial crisis.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Credit derivatives can only be used to hedge credit risk and cannot be used to take on credit exposure, so they cannot contribute to market instability.
cards.explanation: Credit derivatives can also create synthetic credit exposure and leverage, and they have catalysed market disturbances.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the features and use of credit derivatives and discuss potential risks they may create.
cards.statement: Central clearing removes the risk of CDSs because CDSs are more liquid and less risky than other cleared products.
cards.explanation: CDSs are much more illiquid and riskier than other cleared products, so the capacity of CCPs to handle them was untested.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: CCPs contribute to financial stability by providing a structured, regulated environment for managing counterparty risk.
cards.explanation: A CCP replaces bilateral credit exposures with a margined, netted and loss-mutualising structure under common rules, which lowers counterparty and systemic risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: CCPs enhance market liquidity by acting as market makers and setting prices for OTC derivatives.
cards.explanation: A CCP is not a market maker and does not set prices. This confuses clearing with trading or dealing.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: CCPs eliminate market risk in OTC derivatives by standardising the underlying assets.
cards.explanation: Standardisation is a requirement for clearing, but market risk stays with the position holders. A CCP addresses counterparty credit risk only.
cards.originalText: CCPs eliminate market risk in OTC derivatives by standardizing the underlying assets.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: CCPs simplify the legal landscape of OTC derivatives by unifying international regulatory standards across jurisdictions.
cards.explanation: CCPs often operate across borders and face conflicting legal frameworks. They do not unify regulation, and this is listed as a shortfall of CCPs.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: A recognised disadvantage of central clearing is that prioritising the CCP's derivatives counterparties can come at the expense of other creditors, such as bondholders.
cards.explanation: Central clearing gives derivatives counterparties priority protection through collateral. This shifts risk onto non-cleared creditors such as bondholders.
cards.originalText: Prioritizing the CCP’s derivatives counterparties can come at the expense of other creditors, such as bondholders.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Because the CCP replaces the original counterparties, each clearing member's bilateral exposure to its original counterparty is left unchanged.
cards.explanation: Novation replaces the original counterparty with the CCP, so the bilateral exposure to the original counterparty is removed.
cards.originalText: Because the CCP replaces the original counterparties, each clearing member’s bilateral exposure to its original counterparty is left unchanged.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Multilateral netting of offsetting positions increases the net exposure that must be collateralised.
cards.explanation: Multilateral netting reduces net exposures and therefore the collateral required.
cards.originalText: Multilateral netting of offsetting positions increases the net exposure that must be collateralized.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Loss mutualisation concentrates all default losses on the defaulting member's original counterparty.
cards.explanation: Loss mutualisation spreads default losses across all clearing members rather than concentrating them on one counterparty.
cards.originalText: Loss mutualization concentrates all default losses on the defaulting member’s original counterparty.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: A central counterparty (CCP) is a third party that takes responsibility for managing counterparty risk and collateralization, requires standardisation of the contracts it clears, and offers netting benefits and fungibility.
cards.explanation: Central clearing is a natural extension of the exchange model to OTC derivatives. The CCP interposes itself between buyer and seller and uses margining, netting and loss mutualisation.
cards.originalText: Central counterparty (CCP)

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: A primary advantage of central clearing is the mitigation of counterparty credit risk and a lower systemic risk exposure through the CCP's risk-management mechanisms.
cards.explanation: The CCP becomes the counterparty to each trade, and its netting, margining and loss mutualisation reduce counterparty and systemic risk.
cards.originalText: Mitigation of counterparty credit risk and lower systemic risk exposure through CCP risk‑management mechanisms.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Central clearing gives greater flexibility to structure and customise contracts because CCPs accommodate non-standardised instruments.
cards.explanation: Central clearing reduces flexibility because contracts must be standardised. Customisation is a feature of bilateral markets.
cards.originalText: Greater flexibility to structure and customize contracts, since CCPs accommodate non‑standardized instruments.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Central clearing through a CCP eliminates counterparty risk.
cards.explanation: Central clearing significantly reduces counterparty risk relative to bilateral trading but cannot eliminate it. Risk is concentrated in the CCP, and its failure would cause serious losses.
cards.originalText: Elimination of counterparty risk.
cards.correction: Central clearing through a CCP reduces counterparty risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Loss mutualisation is an advantage of using a central counterparty in central clearing.
cards.explanation: Default losses are spread across the clearing members rather than falling on a single counterparty.
cards.originalText: Loss mutualization.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Improved operational efficiency is an advantage of using a central counterparty in central clearing.
cards.explanation: Standardised, centralised processing and orderly close-out of positions improve operational efficiency.
cards.originalText: Improved operational efficiency.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Multilateral netting, which reduces risk, is an advantage of a central counterparty in central clearing.
cards.explanation: Multilateral netting of offsetting positions across members reduces exposures and is a core CCP benefit.
cards.originalText: Risk reduction through multilateral netting.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Centrally cleared markets offer more flexibility in contract selection than bilateral markets.
cards.explanation: Central clearing trades flexibility for standardisation. Contract and collateral choices are narrower than in bilateral markets, where any customised contract can be negotiated.
cards.originalText: offer more flexibility in contract selection.
cards.correction: Centrally cleared markets offer less flexibility in contract selection than bilateral markets.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Centrally cleared markets remain market neutral by netting trades.
cards.explanation: The CCP nets buy-side against sell-side positions, so it carries no net market position.
cards.originalText: remain market neutral by netting trades.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe central clearing of OTC derivatives and discuss the roles, mandate, advantages, and disadvantages of the central counterparty (CCP).
cards.statement: Centrally cleared markets formalise the default close-out process by mutualising losses.
cards.explanation: Central clearing formalises the close-out of a defaulted member's positions, and losses are mutualised across clearing members.
cards.originalText: formalize the default close‑out process by mutualizing losses.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: Margin requirements for centrally cleared derivatives are standardised and enforced by the CCP, whereas non-centrally cleared derivatives involve bilateral agreements with potentially varied margin arrangements.
cards.explanation: The CCP imposes one standardised margin regime on its members. Bilateral margining is agreed between the two counterparties, within regulatory minimums, and so varies.
cards.originalText: Margin requirements for centrally‑cleared derivatives are standardized and enforced by the CCP, whereas non‑centrally‑cleared derivatives involve bilateral agreements with potentially varied margin arrangements.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: Centrally cleared and non-centrally cleared derivatives require exactly the same initial and variation margin, as mandated by global regulatory standards.
cards.explanation: Bilateral margin rules loosely mimic CCP margining but do not equal it. Amounts and terms differ.
cards.originalText: Both centrally‑cleared and non‑centrally‑cleared derivatives require exactly the same initial and variation margin, as mandated by global regulatory standards.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: Margin requirements for centrally cleared derivatives are determined by market makers, whereas those for non-centrally cleared derivatives are set by the individual trading parties.
cards.explanation: Market makers do not set margin. For cleared trades the CCP sets and enforces it.
cards.originalText: Margin requirements for centrally‑cleared derivatives are determined by market makers, while those for non‑centrally‑cleared derivatives are set by the individual trading parties.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: Clearing members of a CCP must post initial margin and variation margin and contribute to a default fund, and regulators have been introducing similar margin requirements for non-centrally cleared bilateral trades.
cards.explanation: Central clearing uses initial margin, variation margin and a default fund. The post-crisis reforms extended similar margin requirements to bilateral trades.
cards.originalText: Clearing members of a CCP must post initial margin and variation margin and contribute to a default fund, and regulators have been introducing similar margin requirements for non‑centrally‑cleared bilateral trades.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: Variation margin is mandatory only for centrally cleared derivatives and remains optional for non-centrally cleared derivatives.
cards.explanation: Variation margin is required for cleared trades and is also now mandated for non-cleared trades, so it is not optional.
cards.originalText: Variation margin is mandatory only for centrally cleared derivatives, and remains entirely optional for non‑centrally‑cleared derivatives.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: Initial margin is not required on centrally cleared trades because the CCP is the counterparty to every trade, but it is required on non-centrally cleared trades.
cards.explanation: Initial margin is required on all cleared trades because it protects the CCP against a member default. It is also now required on bilateral trades.
cards.originalText: Initial margin is not required on centrally cleared trades because the CCP is the counterparty to every trade, but it is required on non‑centrally‑cleared trades.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: Regulators have kept non-centrally cleared derivatives outside margin rules because bilateral OTC trades historically had little or no margin.
cards.explanation: Regulators moved to impose margin on bilateral trades after the crisis, to reduce systemic risk and the incentive to avoid clearing.
cards.originalText: Because bilateral OTC trades historically had little or no margin, regulators have chosen to keep non‑centrally‑cleared derivatives outside margin rules.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: After the 2007-2009 financial crisis, standardised OTC transactions between financial institutions must clear through a CCP, and uncleared trades between financial institutions require both initial and variation margin.
cards.explanation: The reforms have two prongs. The 2009 G20 agreement set a clearing mandate for sufficiently standardised trades, and the 2011 G20 added a margin mandate for non-centrally cleared trades.
cards.originalText: Standardized transactions between financial institutions must clear through a CCP, and uncleared trades between financial institutions require both initial and variation margin.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: The post-crisis regulation of OTC derivatives applied neither to standardised transactions nor to uncleared trades.
cards.explanation: Both categories were newly regulated. Standardised trades face a clearing mandate and uncleared trades face margin requirements.
cards.originalText: The new regulations applied neither to standardized transactions nor to uncleared trades.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: After the 2007-2009 financial crisis, standardised OTC transactions had no new requirements, but uncleared trades between financial institutions must clear through a CCP.
cards.explanation: The logic is reversed. Standardised trades are the ones that must be cleared, and uncleared trades are by definition not cleared and face margin instead.
cards.originalText: Standardized transactions had no new requirements, but uncleared trades between financial institutions must clear through a CCP.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: After the 2007-2009 financial crisis, standardised OTC transactions between financial institutions must clear through a CCP, but uncleared trades are exempt from margin requirements.
cards.explanation: The 2011 G20 mandate specifically added margin requirements for non-centrally cleared derivatives, to give a strong incentive to clear.
cards.originalText: Standardized transactions between financial institutions must clear through a CCP, but uncleared trades are exempt from margin requirements.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: Like monolines and CDPCs, a CCP posts only limited variation margin and typically only in extreme situations such as a rating downgrade.
cards.explanation: Unlike monolines and CDPCs, a CCP imposes margining, both initial and variation, on its members in all situations and runs a matched book.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: A CCP collects variation margin in cash so that it closely tracks market movements.
cards.explanation: Cash variation margin is exchanged regularly and keeps the collateral in line with the market value of positions.
cards.originalText: Variation margin is collected in cash so that it closely tracks market movements.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: A CCP holds initial margin to cover the worst-case liquidation or close-out costs above the variation margin.
cards.explanation: Initial margin protects the CCP against losses that arise between a member's default and the close-out of its positions, beyond what variation margin covers.
cards.originalText: Initial margin is held to cover the worst‑case liquidation or close‑out costs above the variation margin.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Explain the margin requirements for both centrally-cleared and non-centrally-cleared derivatives.
cards.statement: A CCP maintains a default fund to mutualise losses in the event of a severe clearing member default.
cards.explanation: When a defaulter's margin is exhausted, the default fund shares the remaining losses among the clearing members.
cards.originalText: A default fund is maintained to mutualise losses in the event of a severe clearing member default.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the approaches used and the challenges faced in modeling derivatives risk.
cards.statement: Correlations and dependence between risk factors can change substantially, especially in volatile or stressed periods, so a historical estimate may be a poor predictor of future outcomes.
cards.explanation: Historical correlation is backward-looking and unstable. A calm-period estimate can badly misstate dependence in stress, when correlations typically rise.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the approaches used and the challenges faced in modeling derivatives risk.
cards.statement: VaR models ignore dependence between risk factors altogether.
cards.explanation: VaR and expected shortfall models do incorporate correlation and dependence. The weakness is the quality and stability of those inputs, not their absence.
cards.originalText: Historical correlations are unreliable only because VaR ignores dependence between risk factors altogether.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the approaches used and the challenges faced in modeling derivatives risk.
cards.statement: Correlation is irrelevant to credit exposure measures such as potential future exposure, which depend only on the counterparty's default probability.
cards.explanation: Potential future exposure depends on the joint behaviour of market risk factors and on any dependence with default, so correlation matters.
cards.originalText: Correlation is irrelevant to credit exposure measures such as potential future exposure, which depend only on the counterparty’s default probability.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the approaches used and the challenges faced in modeling derivatives risk.
cards.statement: A single correlation number is sufficient to model risk-factor dependence because dependence is stable over time and the same in normal and stressed markets.
cards.explanation: Dependence is not stable. Correlations typically rise in stress, so a single number estimated in calm markets is inadequate.
cards.originalText: A single correlation number is sufficient because dependence between risk factors is stable over time and the same in normal and stressed markets.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the approaches used and the challenges faced in modeling derivatives risk.
cards.statement: Potential future exposure (PFE) is the credit risk analogue of VaR but looks years ahead rather than a few days, which adds complexity and makes the models prone to misinterpretation and misuse.
cards.explanation: Counterparty risk modelling is complex partly because of the long horizon, which makes historical simulation and backtesting harder than for market-risk VaR.
cards.originalText: PFE is the credit risk analogue of VaR but looks years ahead rather than a few days, which adds complexity and makes the models prone to misinterpretation and misuse.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the approaches used and the challenges faced in modeling derivatives risk.
cards.statement: PFE is easier to backtest than VaR because it is measured over a single day.
cards.explanation: PFE horizons are years, not one day. Backtesting is easier for VaR because of its short horizon.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.loText: Describe the approaches used and the challenges faced in modeling derivatives risk.
cards.statement: PFE avoids correlation and dependency problems because it is derived from the counterparty's default probability alone.
cards.explanation: PFE depends on exposure dynamics and on dependence between risk factors, including wrong-way risk, so correlation difficulties are even greater than for VaR.
cards.originalText: PFE avoids correlation and dependency problems because it is derived from the counterparty’s default probability alone.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: An ISDA Master Agreement is a standardised legal framework between two counterparties that sets general terms on netting, collateral, events of default and termination, reducing legal uncertainty and credit risk.
cards.explanation: The terms are agreed once for all OTC trades between the two parties, with indefinite term, so individual trades only need a confirmation.
cards.originalText: It provides a standardized legal framework between two counterparties that sets general terms on netting, collateral, events of default, and termination, reducing legal uncertainty and credit risk.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: An ISDA Master Agreement sets the price, notional and maturity of each individual derivative trade between the counterparties.
cards.explanation: Individual trade economics such as price, notional and maturity are set in trade confirmations. The Master Agreement sets the general legal framework.
cards.originalText: It sets the price, notional, and maturity of each individual derivative trade between the counterparties.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: An ISDA Master Agreement is a regulatory rule issued by authorities that caps the size of OTC derivative positions each party may hold.
cards.explanation: The agreement is a private industry-standard contract, not a regulation, and it sets no position limits.
cards.originalText: It is a regulatory rule issued by authorities that caps the size of OTC derivative positions each party may hold.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: An ISDA Master Agreement is a separate contract for each transaction that is renegotiated from scratch whenever a new trade is added.
cards.explanation: It is one framework covering multiple trades, so adding a new trade does not require renegotiating it.
cards.originalText: It is a separate contract for each transaction that is renegotiated from scratch whenever a new trade is added.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement is a bilateral agreement framework governing OTC derivatives transactions between parties.
cards.explanation: It sets standard terms, such as netting, collateral, default and termination, for the multiple OTC trades between two parties.
cards.originalText: It is a bilateral agreement framework governing OTC derivatives transactions between parties.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement is a regulatory guideline that dictates the trading limits for derivatives.
cards.explanation: It is a private contract, not a regulation, and it sets no trading limits.
cards.originalText: It is a regulatory guideline that dictates the trading limits for derivatives.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement is a mandatory legal document imposed by international trading commissions.
cards.explanation: It is voluntary and privately negotiated between the counterparties, and is not imposed by any commission.
cards.originalText: It is a mandatory legal document imposed by international trading commissions.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement is a framework agreement that sets the standard terms for multiple OTC derivatives transactions between parties.
cards.explanation: One master contract with standard terms covers every OTC trade between the same two parties, which reduces legal uncertainty and credit risk.
cards.originalText: It is a framework agreement that sets the standard terms for multiple OTC derivatives transactions between parties.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement primarily serves as a database for recording all global derivatives transactions.
cards.explanation: It is a contract, not a record database. Trade repositories perform the record-keeping function.
cards.originalText: It primarily serves as a database for recording all global derivatives transactions.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement is an individual contract tailored for single transactional use in derivatives trading.
cards.explanation: It is not single-use. It covers many trades under one agreement, with each new trade added through a confirmation.
cards.originalText: It is an individual contract tailored for single transactional use in derivatives trading.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: All transactions under an ISDA Master Agreement between two counterparties are treated as a single legal whole with a single net value.
cards.explanation: A single legal agreement means all trades form one netting set, so on default only one net value is owed.
cards.originalText: All transactions done under a Master Agreement between two counterparties are treated as a single legal whole with a single net value

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Both counterparties to an ISDA Master Agreement must be domiciled in the United States, because the agreement is not enforceable in other jurisdictions.
cards.explanation: The agreement is used internationally, and legal opinions support netting in many jurisdictions.
cards.originalText: Both counterparties must be domiciled in the United States, as the Master Agreement is not enforceable in other jurisdictions

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Each additional trade between two counterparties generally requires an update to the ISDA Master Agreement.
cards.explanation: The framework has an indefinite term. Each new trade needs only a confirmation, not a change to the Master Agreement.
cards.originalText: Each additional trade between counterparties generally requires an update to the Master Agreement

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: An ISDA Master Agreement mitigates market risk through its mark-to-market provision but mitigates neither counterparty credit risk nor legal risk.
cards.explanation: It is designed to reduce legal uncertainty and credit risk through netting and collateral. It is not a market-risk tool.
cards.originalText: A Master Agreement does mitigate market risk via the mark‑to‑market (MtM) provision but mitigates neither counterparty credit risk nor legal risk

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement includes contractual terms regarding the posting of collateral, the referencing of transactions into single netting sets, the mechanics of the close-out process, and the definitions of events of default.
cards.explanation: These are the standardised contents of the agreement: collateral terms, netting, close-out and events of default and termination.
cards.originalText: The Master Agreement will include contractual terms regarding the posting of collateral, transactions referenced into single netting set(s), close‑out process mechanics, and definitions of events of default

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement mitigates legal risk but cannot be expected to mitigate counterparty risk.
cards.explanation: It mitigates counterparty credit risk too, through close-out netting and collateral provisions.
cards.originalText: Although the ISDA Master Agreement will mitigate legal risk, it cannot be expected to mitigate counterparty risk

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: If an individual transaction produces a trade confirmation, the trade confirmation nullifies the ISDA Master Agreement.
cards.explanation: Confirmations are part of the single agreement and sit under the Master Agreement. They supplement it and do not cancel it.
cards.originalText: If an individual transaction produces a trade confirmation, then the trade confirmation will nullify the Master Agreement

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Explain the purpose of an International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The terms of the ISDA Master Agreement are hard-wired and cannot be adjusted even if both counterparties agree.
cards.explanation: Terms can be tailored by mutual agreement through the Schedule and additional provisions.
cards.originalText: A key drawback of the ISDA Master Agreement is that its terms are ”hard‑wired” and not adjustable even if Zapstreet and the Counterparty both agree

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Within a netting set, expected exposure (EE) and credit value adjustment (CVA) are additive.
cards.explanation: Netting makes exposure non-additive within a netting set, because only the net mark-to-market matters. It is across separate netting sets, which do not offset each other, that exposures add.
cards.originalText: Within a netting set, expected exposure (EE) and credit value adjustment (CVA) are additive
cards.correction: Across netting sets, expected exposure (EE) and credit value adjustment (CVA) are additive.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: A netting set is a set of trades that can be legally netted together in the event of a default.
cards.explanation: This is the definition of a netting set.
cards.originalText: A netting set is a set of trades that can be legally netted together in the event of a default

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Across netting sets exposure is additive, whereas within a netting set the mark-to-market values of trades can be added.
cards.explanation: Separate netting sets do not offset each other, so their exposures add. Within one set, trade values are summed to a single net value.
cards.originalText: Across netting sets, exposure is additive, whereas within a netting set the MtM values of trades can be added

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: A netting set may consist of a single trade, and a counterparty may have more than one netting set.
cards.explanation: A single trade can form its own netting set, and several netting sets can exist with the same counterparty.
cards.originalText: A netting set may consist of a single trade, and a counterparty may have more than one netting set

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Close-out netting terminates all agreements between an insolvent counterparty and a solvent one and offsets the transaction values into a single net amount.
cards.explanation: It combines the right to terminate all contracts on default with the right to offset their values into one claim.
cards.originalText: To terminate all agreements between an insolvent counterparty and a solvent one and offset the transaction values into a single net amount

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Close-out netting nets cash flows falling due on the same day.
cards.explanation: That describes payment netting. Close-out netting is triggered by default and nets the values of terminated transactions.
cards.originalText: To net cash flows falling due on the same day

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Close-out netting terminates all agreements between two parties by compensating only the non-defaulting party while penalising the defaulter.
cards.explanation: Close-out is a calculation of a single net claim. It is not a punitive or one-sided compensation mechanism.
cards.originalText: To terminate all agreements between two parties by compensating only the non‑defaulting party while penalising the defaulter

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Without netting, a surviving party must still settle derivatives with negative values, whereas derivatives with positive values are only a claim in the bankruptcy process.
cards.explanation: Absent netting, the defaulter's estate collects what it is owed while the survivor becomes merely an unsecured creditor on its gains. Exposure is therefore the sum of the positive values.
cards.originalText: derivatives with negative values must be settled, whereas those with positive values are only a claim in the bankruptcy process

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Without netting, derivatives with both positive and negative values must be claimed through the bankruptcy process.
cards.explanation: Only positive-value trades are claims in bankruptcy. The survivor must still pay on the negative-value trades.
cards.originalText: derivatives with both positive and negative values must be claimed through the bankruptcy process

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Netting under ISDA Master Agreements combines cash flows from different contracts into a single net amount, reducing settlement risk and improving operational efficiency.
cards.explanation: Netting replaces many gross payments or claims with one net amount, cutting settlement and credit risk and the operational burden.
cards.originalText: It combines cash flows from different contracts into a single net amount, reducing settlement risk and improving operational efficiency

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Netting under ISDA Master Agreements mainly streamlines tax reporting and simplifies the legal aspects of cross-border trades.
cards.explanation: Tax reporting and cross-border legal simplification are not the purpose of netting. Its purpose is to reduce credit and settlement exposure.
cards.originalText: It mainly streamlines tax reporting and simplifies the legal aspects of cross‑border trades

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Netting under ISDA Master Agreements manages only market risk, aligning the risk profiles of the bank and its counterparties.
cards.explanation: Netting mitigates credit and settlement exposure, not only market risk.
cards.originalText: It manages only market risk, aligning the risk profiles of the bank and its counterparties

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Close-out netting under the ISDA Master Agreement allows the non-defaulting party to terminate all outstanding transactions with the defaulter and net them into a single claim or obligation.
cards.explanation: Close-out netting terminates all contracts and offsets their values into one net amount, unlike acceleration, which only makes future payments immediately due.
cards.originalText: It allows the bank to terminate all outstanding transactions with the defaulter and net them into a single claim or obligation

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Close-out netting reallocates the defaulted trades to other counterparties to maintain market stability.
cards.explanation: Close-out is a bilateral termination process between the two parties. It does not reallocate trades.
cards.originalText: It reallocates the defaulted trades to other counterparties to maintain market stability

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Close-out netting accelerates all future payments due from the defaulting counterparty to give immediate liquidity.
cards.explanation: That describes an acceleration clause, which is distinct from close-out netting. Close-out terminates the transactions and nets their values into one amount.
cards.originalText: It accelerates all future payments due from the defaulting counterparty to give immediate liquidity

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Close-out netting automatically transfers all of a party's positions with the defaulter to a central clearinghouse.
cards.explanation: Transfer to a clearinghouse relates to central clearing and multilateral netting. It is not an automatic result of close-out netting.
cards.originalText: It automatically transfers all of the bank’s positions with the defaulter to a central clearinghouse

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: If a counterparty defaults, the ISDA Master Agreement allows the non-defaulting party to close out and net all outstanding transactions into a single payment obligation, reducing its credit exposure.
cards.explanation: Close-out netting converts many trades into one net claim at default, so exposure is the net amount, not the gross amount.
cards.originalText: If a counterparty bank defaults, the ISDA Master Agreement allows Globex to close out and net all outstanding transactions with that bank into a single payment obligation, reducing its credit exposure.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement eliminates the need to post collateral or margin on OTC derivative transactions.
cards.explanation: The Master Agreement, together with its credit support annex, provides a framework for collateral. It does not remove the need for it.
cards.originalText: The ISDA Master Agreement eliminates the need for Globex to post collateral or margin on its OTC derivative transactions with the banks.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement standardises the pricing and valuation models used for the swaps, so that every transaction is valued consistently.
cards.explanation: ISDA standardises legal terms, not pricing or valuation models. Each party values trades with its own models.
cards.originalText: The ISDA Master Agreement standardizes the pricing and valuation models used for the swaps, so that every transaction with every bank is valued consistently.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: The ISDA Master Agreement removes the non-defaulting party's right to terminate transactions early, so that all swaps continue to maturity after a default.
cards.explanation: The agreement does the opposite. It gives the non-defaulting party the right to terminate and close out all transactions on default.
cards.originalText: The ISDA Master Agreement removes the non‑defaulting party’s right to terminate transactions early, so that all swaps continue to maturity after a default.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Netting can increase the exposure to a given counterparty.
cards.explanation: With netting, exposure is the larger of the net value and zero, which is never greater than the sum of the positive values without netting. Netting either reduces exposure or leaves it unchanged.
cards.correction: Netting cannot increase the exposure to a given counterparty.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: Netting is the right to offset amounts due at termination of individual contracts between the same counterparties when determining the final obligation.
cards.explanation: This is the standard definition of the netting right.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.statement: A disadvantage of multilateral netting is that it tends to mutualise and homogenise counterparty risk, reducing the incentive for institutions to scrutinise counterparty credit quality.
cards.explanation: Mutualisation is the recognised drawback of multilateral netting.
cards.originalText: A disadvantage of multilateral netting is that it tends to mutualize and homogenize counterparty risk, creating a reduced incentive for institutions to scrutinize counterparty credit quality.

cards.subject: Credit Risk
cards.topic: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
cards.loText: Summarize netting and close-out procedures (including multilateral netting), explain their advantages and disadvantages, and describe how they fit into the framework of the ISDA master agreement.
cards.reading: CR-16: Netting, Close-out and Related Aspects
